summary:
--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice says: 'An occasional mistaken action need not erase the possibility of future cooperation.' So we should forgive mistakes, not punish them heavily."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving retaliator that cooperates early, retaliates on defection, forgives isolated defections, and avoids endgame defection. The trace simulates the parent and candidate TFT/adaptive strategies against the listed population slots, focusing on probing, punishment, forgiveness, and last-round exploitation. It proposes changes such as always defecting on the final round, punishing isolated defections, and possibly probing to detect non-retaliators.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So parent's logic of forgiving when opp_defects is low is actually good against slot3." / "So parent is already well-tuned to the population. How can we improve parent?"
STRATEGY: Parent (slot 11) is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy: cooperate first, retaliate immediately in first 10 rounds, forgive early if opp_defects <= max(1, n//10), punish if opp_defects > n*0.3, stern if > n*0.15, and cooperate in endgame if opp_defects <= 2. The trace simulates parent against slot3, slot5, slot0, slot4, slot1, slot7, slot10, and AllD, computing per-round payoffs and totals. Proposed changes: always defect on the last round (n == 99), and retaliate in the endgame (n >= 95 and last_o == 'D' -> return 'D') to prevent late exploitation.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The general advice emphasizes forgiveness: 'An occasional mistaken action need not erase the possibility of future cooperation.' So we should continue to forgive isolated defections, even in endgame, to avoid costly retaliation cycles."
STRATEGY: Parent is a forgiving strategy that cooperates, retaliates only after opponent defections, and forgives isolated defections including in the endgame. The trace simulates parent against slot10, slot3, TFT, AllD, and other population members, computing round-by-round payoffs. It proposes adding an unconditional last-round defection and a round-99 retaliation if the opponent defected at round 98, while otherwise keeping parent's logic.

--- PART 4/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "So the strategy: - Cooperate by default. - If opponent defects, punish according to parent's logic. - If n == 99 (last round): return 'D'. - If n == 98 and last_o == 'D': return 'D' (retaliate to defection at 98). - Otherwise, use parent's logic."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates by default, retaliates/forgives based on opponent defection counts and thresholds, and cooperates in endgame if opp_defects <= 2. Simulated against slot5, slot6, slot7, slot10, slot3, slot8, slot9, AllD, and TFT. Changed by adding unconditional defection at n==99 and retaliation at n==98 if the opponent defected on round 98.
